q: To recover reasoning in low-bit LLMs, existing quantization-aware training (QAT) recipes typically supervise the quantized student with the original full-precision model. On what kind of sequences?
Even after quantization-aware training with existing recipes, on which kind of tasks do low-bit quantized models still struggle?
What is the first of the two challenges the authors identify in closing the gap between the low-bit and full-precision models?
a: trajectory divergence: a mismatch between training prefixes and those encountered during student generation

q: What is the second of the two challenges the authors identify?
a: distributional misalignment: on its own prefixes, the student underpredicts some next-token candidates and overpredicts others

q: OnQ, the authors' low-bit recovery pipeline, combines candidate-wise Dynamic KL with which other technique?
Starting from block-wise calibration, on which prefixes does OnQ's quantized student receive full-precision teacher supervision?
a: its own prefixes, from the responses it generates itself

q: By what does Dynamic KL weight forward and reverse KL?
What does OnQ achieve across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B at 2- and 3-bit precision?
At 2 bits, by how many points does OnQ improve the Qwen3-8B average over the strongest baseline?
What does OnQ also change about the responses it produces?
a: it produces shorter responses with fewer truncations and repetitive errors
